title: The Blaschka Object Network — Dealer Archive Register
scope: Archival survival of the three documented commercial dealers/distributors of Blaschka marine-invertebrate models: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Natural Science Establishment, Robert Damon / Robert Ferris Damon, and Vaclav Fric. The register distinguishes intact business archives from dispersed dealer correspondence preserved by customers, museums and the Blaschka workshop.
methodological_guard: A museum holding objects bought from a dealer is not treated as a dealer archive unless a named correspondence, acquisition, accounts or business-record series can be identified. 'No dedicated corporate fonds identified' means only that this project pass has not located one; it is not a claim that no such records survive anywhere.

status_vocabulary.intact_business_archive: A named personal/business archive survives as a collection of record or corporate archive.
status_vocabulary.distributed_business_correspondence: No dedicated corporate fonds has been identified in this pass; business evidence survives across workshop and customer-side archives.
status_vocabulary.receiving_side_dealer_file: Customer or museum records explicitly document transactions with the dealer.
status_vocabulary.post_blaschka_business_context: Dealer correspondence after marine-model production ended; useful for the firm's wider commercial history but not evidence for a Blaschka transaction by itself.

dealers.name: Henry Augustus Ward / Ward's Natural Science Establishment
dealers.core_repository: Rare Books, Special Collections, and Preservation, University of Rochester
research_value: dealer-side comparison with Dresden workshop accounts
dealers.blaschka_specific_evidence: Corning's global-census research states that United States sales were documented from the Henry A. Ward papers at the University of Rochester. The project's Auckland work also identifies the Ward papers as the highest-value dealer-side target for pricing, shipping, invoice and cancellation evidence.

dealers.name: Robert Damon / Robert Ferris Damon

workshop_side_counterpart.repository: Rakow Research Library, Corning Museum of Glass
workshop_side_counterpart.series: Blaschka business-letter drafts and delivery/order books
workshop_side_counterpart.research_value: Agency terms, prepayment, prices, packing, breakage, institutional orders and disputes. Published archival work identifies Box 13 business-letter drafts and the Lieferungs-Buch as central Damon evidence.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: ten letters created by Robert Damon, 1877-1881, plus one letter to Damon
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Dealer correspondence in the Blaschka era; Blaschka content must be verified item by item.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: Damon correspondence and transaction records across the nineteenth century; named Robert Damon items include DF/ZOO/200/19/70 and DF/ZOO/200/20/106-108, while DF/PAL/100/20/11 is a Robert F. Damon letter from 1884.
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: These files document the museum's commercial relationship with Damon; individual files require inspection before being assigned to Blaschka orders.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: Acquisitions from natural-history dealer Robert Damon, Weymouth, 1873
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Dealer-network context; no Blaschka model content is asserted without file inspection.

distributed_archival_witnesses.repository: Museum of New Zealand Te Papa Tongarewa Archives
distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: Robert Damon letter, 1 March 1889, concerning dispersal of the Godfrey Collection
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Late dealer-business context; not a Blaschka transaction by itself.

critical_gaps: A dedicated Damon firm archive, order book or invoice series has not been located in this pass.
The Damon letter that prompted the Blaschkas' 2 November 1886 agency reply was reported missing in published NHM research.
Customer-side Damon files need item-level inspection for Blaschka catalogue lists, prices, packing and remittances.

dealers.name: Vaclav Fric / V. Fric natural-history and teaching-aids business
dealers.business_history_guard: The firm continued under Jaromir Fric after Vaclav Fric and ended in 1959. The National Museum in Prague received remaining natural-history stock; this transfer of stock is not treated as proof that a complete company paper archive was transferred.

workshop_side_counterpart.repository: Rakow Research Library, Corning Museum of Glass
workshop_side_counterpart.series: Blaschka business notebooks and letter drafts
workshop_side_counterpart.notable_item: 8 November 1884 draft to Vaclav Fric concerning a commercial shipment and four glass models sent as a gift to the Prague museum
workshop_side_counterpart.research_value: Reseller relations, shipment composition, gifts, catalogue commerce and workshop-side dealer correspondence.

distributed_archival_witnesses.collection: Trustee Minutes, Outward Letter Books and purchase-of-specimens correspondence
distributed_archival_witnesses.evidence: The museum's archival reconstruction found the 1879 instruction to Fric to obtain Blaschka glass invertebrates and later correspondence about three mixed consignments.

distributed_archival_witnesses.collection: Museum accession books and institutional records
distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: 1884 Fric-mediated delivery of four Blaschka models
distributed_archival_witnesses.evidence: Published reconstruction joins the 8 November 1884 workshop draft to the National Museum accession book, which records Fric's delivery.

distributed_archival_witnesses.reference: Dealer-specific acquisition file listed as 'Erwerbungen beim Naturalienhändler V. Fric (Prag)'
distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: nineteenth-century dealer acquisition records; exact Blaschka content pending inspection
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: The finding aid proves a dedicated Fric acquisition file at the receiving institution, not that it contains Blaschka models.

distributed_archival_witnesses.coverage: three items from V. Fric, Prague, 1905
distributed_archival_witnesses.blaschka_guard: Post-production business context only unless item content establishes an earlier collection link.

critical_gaps: A dedicated V. Fric company correspondence/account archive has not been identified in this pass.
The relationship between surviving company stock transferred to the National Museum in 1959 and surviving business papers remains unresolved.
Dealer-side order books, invoices and customer ledgers would be the decisive source for reconstructing the Austria-Hungary network at scale.

network_observation: The archival asymmetry is itself significant: Ward has an identifiable personal and corporate archive, while Damon and Fric currently have to be reconstructed from the Blaschka workshop archive plus customer-side correspondence and acquisition files. A dealer-network history therefore requires provenance across archival institutions rather than treating 'the dealer archive' as a single repository.
